question: Around w00's own +0 on the known-text window, do blind humans confirm the agents' depth budget (outward < 12 um), s214732's 'no rows', and the 20 mm field size?
window: PHerc0841 known-text window W on w00 (20 x 11.7 mm), canonical 2.4 um reader, fixed clip(0,1) x 255 mapping
sign: + = outward (away from the scroll centre: 99.9 % of w00's normals); - = inward, toward s214732

levels_20mm.ctrl: readable control: w00 at its own +0 (byte copy of partsheet L100)
levels_20mm.out12: w00 shifted uniformly +5 layers (+12 um, outward = away from the scroll centre)
levels_20mm.out24: w00 shifted uniformly +10 layers (+24 um outward)
levels_20mm.in12: w00 shifted uniformly -5 layers (-12 um, inward)
levels_20mm.in24: w00 shifted uniformly -10 layers (-24 um inward)
levels_20mm.s214732: the organizers' second auto-grown surface of this region, s214732, about 66 um inward along w00's normal (78 um from w00)

pictures.blanks_20mm: one wrong-order blank per 20 mm level (6)
pictures.windows_10mm: three 10 x 10 mm windows (top / middle / bottom, 50 % overlap) of the w00 control map and of s214732's map, plus one blank each (middle, wrong order); 12.5 um per tile pixel vs 25 um at 20 mm (sampled 2x finer)
pictures.calib: calibration: a known-rows ink map of another public fragment's known text (not this window), a picture both raters had rated before
pictures.calib_blank: the calibration map in the wrong layer order (wrong-order blank)

page_order: hardest first, shuffled inside blocks (numpy default_rng 20261007): A = the 4 shifted levels + s214732 + their blanks; B = the six 10 mm windows + 2 blanks; C = ctrl + blank, calibration, calibration blank

rule.valid_rater: all 22 answered; calibration rows; at most 1 of the 8 surface blanks (6 at 20 mm, 2 at 10 mm) rows; the calibration blank reported, not gating
rule.countable: a level counts only if its own blank is not rows for that rater (else uncountable)

per_rater_20mm.VOID: ctrl not rows, or ctrl's blank rows, or invalid rater
per_rater_20mm.WIDE-OUT: out12 or out24 reads rows (outward line = furthest outward tile with rows)
per_rater_20mm.INCOMPLETE: else, out12 or out24 uncountable (or an inward tile needed for the call uncountable)
per_rater_20mm.ASYMMETRIC: else in24 rows -> 'outward < 12 um, inward >= 24 um'
per_rater_20mm.ASYMMETRIC-SHORT: else in12 rows, in24 not -> 'outward < 12, inward 12-24 um'
per_rater_20mm.NARROW: else +-12 both not rows -> '< 12 um both sides'
per_rater_20mm.non-monotone flag: out24 rows with out12 not (or in24 rows with in12 not): keep the furthest tile, flag it

rule.two_raters: per side the stricter (narrower) line, both printed; the outcome name follows the combined lines; a rater whose call is INCOMPLETE is reported tile by tile and the combined call uses the other rater ('one rater')
rule.s214732: rows / not rows per rater (uncountable if its blank reads rows); all countable valid raters not rows -> confirmed 'does not read'; all rows -> the agent-only 'does not read' line is removed; otherwise SPLIT
rule.unit_10mm: per rater k_P / k_S = w00's / s214732's windows read rows (0-3): '1 cm2 USABLE' if k_P >= 2 and k_S = 0; '20 mm ONLY' if k_P = 0 or k_S >= k_P; otherwise DESCRIPTIVE; uncountable if either 10 mm blank reads rows; two raters: a named unit only if both agree (else DESCRIPTIVE / SPLIT)

scope: one 20 x 12 mm window, one tile per arm, depth measured from w00's own +0 (not from the inked layer); the 10 mm block is sampled 2x finer and is descriptive only
